precepts.text: Awake, put on thy strength O Zion, put on thy beautiful garments O Jerusalem the holy city.
precepts.point: The Most High has chosen Zion for his habitation. Zion is called the city of David, but Zion also refers to a people, the Israelites.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “For the Lord hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation.” Zion is called the city of David, but Zion also refers to a people, the Israelites: “Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean.” A city does not awake and put on strength; a people does.

note.label: CHRIST THE GOD THE REDEEMER

precepts.why:
“As concerning therefore the eating of those things that are offered in sacrifice unto idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world”. An idol is nothing.

So when Isaiah 52:3 says “Ye have sold yourselves for nought”, it means we sold ourselves for idols. By worshipping idols and going after other gods we allowed ourselves to be sold, and the curses came upon us.

note.label: CHRIST THE GOD THE REDEEMER

precepts.why:
To show what being redeemed with money is: “Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of their cattle; and the Levites shall be mine: I am the Lord.” The Levites belong to the Lord. For the firstborn over and above the number of the Levites, “Thou shalt even take five shekels apiece by the poll, after the shekel of the sanctuary”, “And thou shalt give the money, wherewith the odd number of them is to be redeemed, unto Aaron and to his sons.”

You had to give money to be redeemed. Every firstborn brought into this world had to pay money to be redeemed according to the law. “And Moses took the redemption money”, “And Moses gave the money of them that were redeemed unto Aaron and to his sons, according to the word of the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.” This was the law kept concerning every firstborn in Israel: that soul had to be redeemed with money.

There is a reason the firstborn had to be redeemed with money, and the Lord says the firstborn belongs to him, but that is for another time.

note.label: CHRIST THE GOD THE REDEEMER

precepts.why:
“Every thing that openeth the matrix in all flesh, which they bring unto the Lord, whether it be of men or beasts, shall be thine”. The matrix is the woman’s womb, the portal into this world. “Nevertheless the firstborn of man shalt thou surely redeem, and the firstling of unclean beasts shalt thou redeem. And those that are to be redeemed from a month old shalt thou redeem, according to thine estimation, for the money of five shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs.”

These things are a shadow of things to come. For every firstborn a price, money, had to be paid for that soul to be redeemed, and all of that goes into something spiritual: the firstborn, the firstfruits, the best of the best, the firstborn of many brethren. Under the law you had to pay money to be redeemed or purchased unto the Lord. That is why it stands out that Isaiah says we are redeemed without money.

note.label: CHRIST THE GOD THE REDEEMER

precepts.why:
See what Judas Maccabeus did. Judas called upon the Lord to be their helper and leader of the battle, and rushing upon Gorgias’ men, “he put them to flight.” “And when the seventh day came, they purified themselves, as the custom was, and kept the sabbath in the same place.” The day following they came to take up the bodies of their brothers that were slain, “and to bury them with their kinsmen in their fathers’ graves.”

“Now under the coats of every one that was slain they found things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Jews by the law. Then every man saw that this was the cause wherefore they were slain.” These brothers had idols under their clothing, and that is why the Lord allowed them to die in that battle. Judas and his men prayed for them, “that the sin committed might wholly be put out of remembrance”, and Judas exhorted the people to keep themselves from sin.

“And when he had made a gathering throughout the company to the sum of two thousand drachms of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering”, “in that he was mindful of the resurrection”. Judas Maccabeus and our forefathers understood the resurrection: “For if he had not hoped that they that were slain should have risen again, it had been superfluous and vain to pray for the dead.” “Whereupon he made a reconciliation for the dead, that they might be delivered from sin.”

He made that reconciliation by sending the money up. By the law, he tried to redeem those brothers with money: the same money paid for every firstborn to redeem their soul. But Israel shall be redeemed without money.

note.label: CHRIST THE GOD THE REDEEMER

precepts.why:
We shall be redeemed, brought back and freed without money. “What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price”.

We are not our own; we are bought. When Deuteronomy 28:68 says no man shall buy you, none of our brothers or our leaders was able to buy us or free us from captivity and oppression, or redeem us. But Christ came and died and paid that price for us. Christ is the one that bought us; he redeemed us and bought us with a price.

note.label: CHRIST THE GOD THE REDEEMER

precepts.why:
What is that price? “And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver.”

Thirty pieces of silver is what they paid to kill Christ, our King. That was his price, what they gave his brother Judas to deliver him up to be killed.

note.label: CHRIST THE GOD THE REDEEMER

precepts.why:
“And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.” Those thirty pieces of silver were the price of Christ’s blood.

So when it says we are bought with a price, the price is the blood of Christ. That is the payment for us to be let go from slavery, the payment for our freedom: his blood is what he used to buy us back. No man was able to buy us or free us, but with his blood Christ paid the price to redeem us.

note.label: CHRIST THE GOD THE REDEEMER

precepts.why:
“Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold”. We were not bought, purchased or freed with corruptible things. We sold ourselves for nought and shall be redeemed without money. Silver and gold is what was read in the Old Testament: every firstborn that came out of the matrix had to be redeemed with money, and Judas Maccabeus sent shekels up to Jerusalem and prayed for the brothers that died in sin.

“From your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers”. The tradition of the fathers is what was read in Leviticus and Numbers: the shekels, the money paid to the priest in the temple to redeem every firstborn. We were not redeemed with those things.

“But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot”. That is how we are freed, how we were bought: the price we were bought with is Christ’s blood. He is that lamb without blemish and without spot, meaning he walked perfect on this earth, without sin, and we are redeemed through his blood. No man would be able to save us, redeem us or free us, but Christ purchased us with his blood.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 21 Thy Kingdom Come

precepts.why: “Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion”: he’s telling us to wake up and put on our strength. “Put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city”: how is a city going to put on garments? This city represents the people. “There shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean”: meaning the other nations.

moments.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: My people is taken away for nought: they that rule over them make them to howl, saith the Lord; and my name continually every day is blasphemed.

His name is blasphemed every day, all around the world. The false image of Christ is blasphemy. He died for all people is blasphemy against what is written. He does not exist, atheism, evolution: blasphemy. His name and reputation are spoken evil of continually.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Zion is called to awake and put on strength, and Jerusalem the holy city to put on her beautiful garments, for henceforth the uncircumcised and the unclean shall no more come into her. She is told to shake off the dust, arise, and loose the bands of her neck.

note.label: Isaiah 52: Awake, Zion, Redeemed Without Money

points: They sold themselves for nothing and shall be redeemed without money. His people went down into Egypt to sojourn, and the Assyrian oppressed them without cause.

note.label: Isaiah 52: Awake, Zion, Redeemed Without Money

points: Because those that rule over them make them howl and his name is blasphemed continually every day, his people shall therefore know his name, and know in that day that he is the one who speaks.

note.label: Isaiah 52: Awake, Zion, Redeemed Without Money

points: Beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that brings good tidings, that publishes peace and salvation and says to Zion, Thy God reigneth. The watchmen shall lift up the voice and sing together when they see eye to eye and the Lord brings again Zion.

note.label: Isaiah 52: Awake, Zion, Redeemed Without Money

points: The waste places of Jerusalem are told to break forth into joy, for the Lord has comforted his people and redeemed Jerusalem, making bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations, so all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.

note.label: Isaiah 52: Awake, Zion, Redeemed Without Money

points: They are told to depart and go out from thence, touching no unclean thing and being clean that bear the vessels of the Lord; they shall not go out in haste or by flight, for the Lord will go before them and be their rearward.

note.label: Isaiah 52: Awake, Zion, Redeemed Without Money

points: The Servant shall deal prudently and be exalted, extolled, and made very high. Many were astonished at him because his visage was marred more than any man and his form more than the sons of men.

note.label: Isaiah 52: Awake, Zion, Redeemed Without Money

points: So shall he sprinkle many nations, and kings shall shut their mouths at him, for what had not been told them they shall see, and what they had not heard they shall consider.

note.label: Isaiah 52: Awake, Zion, Redeemed Without Money

points: The Most High said his hand is not short that he cannot save us and redeem us. “Shake thyself from the dust”: in these lands we have been under the dust, laid down on the floor with the nations walking upon us, and God says shake yourself from it. “Arise”: wake up to who you are; you are the sons of God. “And sit down, O Jerusalem: loose thyself from the bands of thy neck”. The bands of our neck are this captivity, and the lies and philosophies we learned here in slavery.

“O captive daughter of Zion”: the daughters of Zion are captives in the different lands we were scattered to as slaves. Some of you don’t have the yoke on your neck, but you are still captive. Some think they are free; no, we are still captives, in the land of our captivity.

note.label: CHRIST THE GOD THE REDEEMER

points: “For thus saith the Lord, Ye have sold yourselves for nought”. We sold ourselves for nought by worshipping idols, going after other gods. We allowed ourselves to be sold: because we worshipped idols and went against our God, these curses came upon us and we were scattered throughout the four corners of the earth as slaves.

“And ye shall be redeemed without money.” To redeem is to free, to buy. The Lord is going to make a purchase and buy us back, but he is not going to use money to redeem us. Under the law every firstborn needed money to be redeemed, and Judas Maccabeus sent silver up to Jerusalem for his slain brothers, but we are redeemed, bought and freed without money. No man could buy us; Christ bought us, and the price is his blood.
